_note: Social engine configuration. Pure data — no secrets, no absolute paths.

inbox._note: Drop zone. One directory per item, with an optional item.json (title, kind, description, tags, publish, price).

reels._note: Reels the reel-watcher already produced, in the flat layout it writes: <base>.mp4, <base>_cover.jpg and <base>_POST.md in one directory (the parked <base>_source.mp4 is not a reel).

catalogue._note: The store's catalogue: cover studies, System Error plates and the daily bundle the daily run publishes (assets/marketplace/daily/<date>/plates.json). Metadata comes from lettering-manifest.json / plates.json.

posting._note_enabled: Master switch for handing a package to lib/ig-poster.js. The poster is the only thing that publishes, and it publishes to a real account — so the second switch matters more.
posting._note_autoPublish: false = a package is staged unless the item opts in (publish: true in its item.json). true = every packaged item is posted. A public post is irreversible; the opt-in is the gate.
posting._note_dryRunPoster: true = the worker still runs the poster, but with --dry-run. This is how the handoff is smoke-tested without publishing.

twitter._note_enabled: false = X is never posted to, even when the item opts in. A tweet on a personal account is the least reversible thing this repo does, so it takes a deliberate edit to arm it — and it needs a valid session cookie (see docs/X-COOKIES.md).
twitter._note_dryRunPoster: true = the worker runs the X poster with --dry-run: it reads the package, reports the caption it would post, and stops. Nothing is published and no browser is opened — the same shape as the Instagram poster's dry run.

price._note_bundleDiscount: The bundle is the whole catalogue at a fifth off — a real price decision, computed from the item prices rather than typed in.
